open_points.subject: A08 Required test 8
open_points.text: A proposal whose input and output ports are given out of name order is recorded, and the answer is that one binding with its ports in name order; another proposal of the same operation already in the store is not the answer.
open_points.question: Is the recording guarantee limited to a proposal that passes every refusal check in A08 rule 5, or must out-of-order ports cause recording even when another check requires refusal?
options: Qualify the result: an otherwise valid proposal is recorded after its ports are ordered.
Make port ordering override the refusal checks and record such a proposal.
State a different precedence between normalization and each refusal check.
open_points.default_guess: Qualify the result to an otherwise valid proposal; rule 5 continues to refuse a proposal that fails any of its checks.

witness.initial: The manifest contains an invocable operation; an agent prepares a proposal whose ports are listed as b, a and whose output omits the disclosure class required by M01 and A08 rule 5.
events: The agent submits the proposal with its ports out of name order.
The kernel applies A08 rule 5 and Required test 8.
outcomes: A08 rule 5 refuses the proposal and records no binding because a required port class is absent.
Required test 8 records the proposal and returns a binding with ordered ports because its ports were supplied out of name order.
witness.observer: The proposing agent sees either a refusal or a returned binding, and the store either lacks or contains the binding.

open_points.subject: A08 port canonicalization
open_points.text: A proposal whose input and output ports are given out of name order is recorded, and the answer is that one binding with its ports in name order; another proposal of the same operation already in the store is not the answer.
open_points.question: What exact total order defines “name order” for the input and output port lists?
options: Unicode code-point lexicographic order, as explicitly used elsewhere for identifiers and port names.
Locale-independent natural order, so numeric substrings compare numerically.
Another explicitly defined bytewise or case-normalized order.
open_points.default_guess: Order each direction separately by port name using Unicode code-point lexicographic order.

witness.initial: An otherwise valid operation proposal has input ports named a2 and a10, supplied in the order a2, a10.
events: The kernel decides whether the supplied order is already “name order” and records the returned binding.
outcomes: Unicode code-point lexicographic ordering returns the ports as a10, a2.
Natural-name ordering returns the ports as a2, a10.
witness.observer: The proposing agent sees the different port order in the returned binding; later readers of the stored binding see the same difference.
